revision.actions-yaml:
get-admin-password:
  description: 'Get the dashboard url and initial admin password for the Grafana web
    interface. Initial

    admin password is generated at charm deployment time. If the password has been
    changed,

    a notice of that fact will be returned by this action instead.

    '
revision.config-yaml:
options:
  admin_roles:
    description: 'Unquoted, comma-separated list of groups oAuth2/OIDC that should
      be granted admin

      privileges in Grafana. Only applicable when using oAuth2/OIDC authentication.


      Example:

      juju config grafana admin_roles="admin,another-group"

      '
    type: string
  admin_user:
    default: admin
    description: The Grafana administrative user
    type: string
  allow_anonymous_access:
    default: false
    description: 'Whether Grafana should allow anonymous access to dashboards. Unless

      you have some other authentication mechanism in front of your deployment,

      you likely do not want to enable this.

      '
    type: boolean
  allow_embedding:
    default: false
    description: 'Whether Grafana should allow embedding dashboards using iframes.
      Unless

      you have a clear reason for doing so, you likely do not want to enable this.

      '
    type: boolean
  cpu:
    description: 'K8s cpu resource limit, e.g. "1" or "500m". Default is unset (no
      limit). This value is used

      for the "limits" portion of the resource requirements (the "requests" portion
      is

      automatically deduced from it).

      See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

      '
    type: string
  custom_config:
    description: "Additional configuration options to be added to grafana.ini.\nThese\
      \ options will be appended to the grafana.ini file, allowing for custom configuration.\n\
      Note that this config option accepts only a small subset of the grafana.ini\
      \ file.\nCurrently supported sections:\n- [smtp], ref: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#smtp\n\
      \nTo set this configuration, create a local INI file and pass it using the @file\
      \ syntax:\n\n  juju config grafana-k8s custom_config=@smtp-config.ini\n\nSensitive\
      \ values can be referenced from Juju secrets using a `secret://<secret-id>/<key>`\n\
      URL in place of the plaintext value. The secret must exist in the same model\
      \ and be\ngranted to the charm with `juju grant-secret`. For example:\n\n  juju\
      \ add-secret smtp-config password=\"my-smtp-password\"\n  juju grant-secret\
      \ smtp-config grafana-k8s\n\n  cat > smtp-config.ini <<EOF\n  [smtp]\n  enabled\
      \ = true\n  password = secret://<secret-id>/password\n  EOF\n  juju config grafana-k8s\
      \ custom_config=@smtp-config.ini\n"
    type: string
  datasource_query_timeout:
    default: 300
    description: 'The default timeout for querying a Grafana datasource. Each datasource
      can

      also configure its own preferred timeout value through relation data. If the

      value configured through relation data is larger than datasource_query_timeout

      then that value is left unchanged. The value of this configuration option must

      be a positive integer representing the maximum number of seconds Grafana will

      wait for a datasource to respond to a query.

      '
    type: int
  editor_roles:
    description: 'Unquoted, comma-separated list of groups oAuth2/OIDC that should
      be granted editor

      privileges in Grafana. Only applicable when using oAuth2/OIDC authentication.


      Example:

      juju config grafana editor_roles="devs,another-group"

      '
    type: string
  enable_auto_assign_org:
    default: true
    description: 'Set to true to automatically add new users to the main organization
      (id 1). When set to

      false, new users automatically cause a new organization to be created for that
      new user.

      '
    type: boolean
  log_level:
    default: info
    description: "Logging level for Grafana. Options are \u201Cdebug\u201D, \u201C\
      info\u201D,\n\u201Cwarn\u201D, \u201Cerror\u201D, and \u201Ccritical\u201D.\n"
    type: string
  memory:
    description: 'K8s memory resource limit, e.g. "1Gi". Default is unset (no limit).
      This value is used

      for the "limits" portion of the resource requirements (the "requests" portion
      is

      automatically deduced from it).

      See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

      '
    type: string
  reporting_enabled:
    default: true
    description: 'When disabled, Grafana will be configured to not send anonymous
      usage statistics to stats.grafana.org, nor

      periodically check for updates.

      It is very helpful to the Grafana project, so please leave this enabled.


      When enabled, Grafana will use its default values for analytics.


      Ref: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#analytics

      '
    type: boolean
  web_external_url:
    default: ''
    description: 'DEPRECATED. This config option is no longer used, in favor of "skipPrefix".


      The URL under which Grafana is externally reachable (for example,

      if Grafana is served via a reverse proxy).


      Used for generating relative and absolute links back to

      Grafana itself. If the URL has a path portion, it will be used to

      prefix all HTTP endpoints served by Grafana.


      If omitted, relevant URL components will be derived automatically.


      If provided, this should be a complete URI, including scheme, or a

      fully qualified subpath starting with `/`.


      If Grafana is being served directly from the root of a fully-qualified

      host or a bare A record, this may be omitted.

      '
    type: string
revision.metadata-yaml:
assumes:
- k8s-api
- juju >= 3.6
containers:
  grafana:
    mounts:
    - location: /var/lib/grafana
      storage: database
    resource: grafana-image
description: "Grafana K8s is a Juju charm that deploys and manages Grafana on Kubernetes.\
  \ It provides a\nweb interface for visualizing and exploring observability data\
  \ and is a core component\nof the Canonical Observability Stack (COS):\nhttps://documentation.ubuntu.com/observability\n\
  \nDatasources such as Prometheus and Loki, as well as dashboards bundled by other\
  \ charms, are\nautomatically registered through Juju relations \u2014 no manual\
  \ configuration required.\n\nKey features:\n\n- Automatic datasource and dashboard\
  \ registration via Juju relations with charms such as\n  Prometheus, Loki, and others\
  \ in the COS ecosystem.\n- High-availability support using a PostgreSQL database\
  \ backend.\n- OAuth2/OIDC authentication via the oauth relation, with configurable\
  \ role mappings.\n- TLS support via the certificates relation.\n- Ingress support\
  \ for external access through reverse proxies such as Traefik.\n- Built-in Prometheus\
  \ alert rules for self-monitoring.\n- Distributed tracing support via integration\
  \ with Tempo.\n- Configurable Kubernetes resource limits for CPU and memory.\n"
docs: https://documentation.ubuntu.com/observability/latest/
issues:
- https://github.com/canonical/grafana-k8s-operator/issues
name: grafana-k8s
peers:
  grafana:
    interface: grafana_peers
  replicas:
    interface: grafana_replicas
provides:
  grafana-metadata:
    description: 'Provides metadata about the grafana instance, such as its URL and
      ID.

      '
    interface: grafana_metadata
    optional: true
  metrics-endpoint:
    description: Links to grafana's own `/metrics` endpoint.
    interface: prometheus_scrape
    optional: true
  profiling-endpoint:
    description: 'Links to grafana''s pprof endpoint. Can be used to integrate with
      parca to

      profile the grafana server process.

      '
    interface: parca_scrape
    optional: true
  provide-cmr-mesh:
    description: 'Access a cross-model application from this charm via the service
      mesh.

      This relation provides additional data required by the service mesh to enforce
      cross-model authorization policies.

      '
    interface: cross_model_mesh
requires:
  catalogue:
    interface: catalogue
    optional: true
  certificates:
    description: Certificate and key files for Grafana to use with TLS.
    interface: tls-certificates
    limit: 1
    optional: true
  charm-tracing:
    description: 'Enables sending charm traces to a distributed tracing backend such
      as Tempo.

      '
    interface: tracing
    limit: 1
    optional: true
  grafana-auth:
    interface: grafana_auth
    optional: true
  grafana-dashboard:
    interface: grafana_dashboard
    optional: true
  grafana-source:
    interface: grafana_datasource
    optional: true
  ingress:
    interface: ingress
    limit: 1
    optional: true
  logging:
    description: 'Receives Loki''s push api endpoint address to push logs to, and
      forwards charm''s built-in alert rules to Loki.

      '
    interface: loki_push_api
    optional: true
  oauth:
    description: 'Receive oauth server''s info and a set of client credentials.

      This relation can be used to integrate grafana with an oAuth2/OIDC Provider.

      '
    interface: oauth
    limit: 1
    optional: true
  pgsql:
    description: 'This endpoint allows using a PostgreSQL database backend for data
      storage.

      Using this endpoint overrides Grafana''s usage of the embedded sqlite3 database

      for data storage and is required for more than one Grafana unit.

      '
    interface: postgresql_client
    limit: 1
    optional: true
  receive-ca-cert:
    description: 'Receive a CA cert for grafana to trust.

      This relation can be used with a local CA to obtain the CA cert that was used
      to sign proxied

      endpoints.

      '
    interface: certificate_transfer
    optional: true
  require-cmr-mesh:
    description: 'Allow a cross-model application access to this charm via the service
      mesh.

      This relation provides additional data required by the service mesh to enforce
      cross-model authorization policies.

      '
    interface: cross_model_mesh
  service-mesh:
    description: 'Subscribe this charm to a service mesh and create authorization
      policies.

      '
    interface: service_mesh
    limit: 1
  workload-tracing:
    description: 'Enables sending workload traces to a distributed tracing backend
      such as Tempo.

      '
    interface: tracing
    limit: 1
    optional: true
resources:
  grafana-image:
    description: upstream docker image for Grafana
    type: oci-image
    upstream-source: docker.io/ubuntu/grafana@sha256:1af2d3519cc3515708f855909a3a5329404079fd50d1cf6b69a7de40067447c4
source:
- https://github.com/canonical/grafana-k8s-operator
storage:
  database:
    type: filesystem
summary: Data visualization and observability with Grafana
website:
- https://charmhub.io/grafana-k8s
